title: Tinto Brass, Director of the X-Rated ‘Caligula,’ Dies at 93
full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 8:38am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tinto Brass Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images Tinto Brass, the Italian director best known for helming the X-rated Roman Empire epic Caligula , starring Malcolm McDowell, died Wednesday in Rome, his family announced. He was 93. Brass started out in the 1960s with avant-garde films before he pivoted to erotic cinema, with his other features in the genre including Salon Kitty (1976), The Key (1983), Paprika (1991), All Ladies Do It (1992), Frivolous Lola (1998) and Cheeky (2000). McDowell starred in the title role as the sexually deranged emperor in Caligula (1979), written by Gore Vidal and produced by Penthouse magazine founder Bob Guccione. The film, also featuring Helen Mirren, Peter O’Toole , John Gielgud and lots of orgies, was slammed by critics and audiences after its original release. Related Stories Oscars 2027: Int'l Films in Focus 'Ulya' Director Dives Into His Third Latvian Oscar Contender, Which Stars a Rising Actor as a Female Basketball Legend and Became a "Blockbuster" Movies BAFTA Breakthrough Ted Evans Shares What Sign Language Taught Him About Film - and What's Next After 'Retreat' Brass and Vidal clashed during production and would disown the feature — the director was unhappy with the editing (done after he was fired), the screenwriter with how Brass rewrote his script. Caligula , however, gained a cult following over the decades, and a 178-minute “ultimate cut” version received a showcase at Cannes in 2023. Born in Milan on March 26, 1933, and raised in Venice, Giovanni Brass earned a law degree, worked as an archivist at the Cinémathèque Française in Paris and served as an assistant director to Roberto Rossellini and Alberto Cavalcanti. He made his feature directorial debut on Who Works Is Lost , which screened at the 1963 Venice International Film Festival, then helmed Yankee (1966), a Western, and the murder mystery I Am What I Am (1967), starring Jean-Louis Trintignant . (The last one received a 4K restoration and a screening at Venice in September.) In 1970s, he won the Golden Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival for his surrealist comedy The Howl , which he also wrote. Survivors include his second wife, Caterina, whom he married in 2017, and his children, Bonifacio and Beatrice. His first wife was Carla Cipriani; he was married to the daughter of Harry’s Bar founder Giuseppe Cipriani from 1957 until her death in 2006. THR

title: ‘Red, White & Royal Blue’ Author Responds To Texas Going Blue In Midterms: “It Was All In The Binder”
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Paramount+ Drama Slate: Series Moving To HBO, Sarah Aubrey & Francesca Orsi Sharing Oversight Among Options Explored Post-Merger – The Dish Chanel Pysnik Departing As Head Of Nonfiction For Prince Harry & Meghan Markle’s Archewell Prods. Netflix Orders ‘Prep’ YA Series Based On Book From ‘One Day’ EP Nicole Taylor & Gloria Sanchez Prods. View All November 4, 2026 8:37am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Taylor Zakhar Perez in 'Red, White & Royal Blue'; U.S. Sen.-elect James Talarico Amazon Studios/Getty Texas made history Tuesday night during the midterms when James Talarico became the state’s first Democratic Senator since 1988, defeating Republican Ken Paxton. The flip may have come as a shock for many, but Red, White & Royal Blue fans saw it as a prophecy coming to life. In author Casey McQuiston ‘s popular 2019 novel and Prime Video’s 2023 film adaptation, Alex Claremont-Diaz ( Taylor Zakhar Perez ) is the son of America’s first female president, Democrat Ellen Claremont, played in the film by Uma Thurman, who is facing a tough reelection. Related Stories News Midterm Elections: Democrats Take Control Of Congress, Riding Big Wins In Texas, Michigan, Georgia & Maine Politics Midterm Elections: Amid The Blue Tsunami, A Night Of Many Firsts In a 14-page memo, aka the Texas Binder, Alex laid out an ambitious political strategy to turn his home state of Texas blue. It looked like a long shot, but he got a chance to implement it. In the end, the vote came down to Texas, which defied projections by going blue, securing Ellen a second term. Red, White & Royal Blue fans flooded social media after Talarico was announced as the winner, touting “the Alex Claremont-Diaz impact” on his victory. “It was all in the binder,” McQuiston wrote in response to Vulture’s IG post featuring a photo of Zakhar Perez as Alex with the caption “History, huh? #iykyk.” At Deadline’s Contenders Television held during the last election year, 2024, we asked Zakhar Perez and Red, White & Royal Blue producer Sarah Schechter which they think we’ll see first in our lifetime: an openly gay British prince or Texas going blue again? ( Red, White & Royal Blue follows the romance between Alex and a British Prince, played by Nicholas Galitzine, who comes out as gay.) “That is an excellent, excellent question. I really hope for both, I really just hope for both,” Schechter said back in April 2024 when Joe Biden was still the Democratic Presidential candidate. Added Zakhar Perez, “I think Joe needs to read Alex’s memo.” (You can watch the exchange towards the end of the video below.) Biden and his replacement Kamala Harris may not have read the memo, but Talarico clearly did. The Red, White & Royal Blue sequel, Red White & Royal Wedding, has been shot and is awaiting a release date by Prime Video. Bass & Raman In Dead Heat For L.A. title: Nick Hall Strikes Producing Deal With Vice Studios
full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter Toni Collette To Star In TV Adaptation Of Norwegian Dramedy ‘Pernille’ For Apple Sharon Horgan’s ‘Youth’ Renewed For Season 2 At HBO Sandy Frank Dies: Legendary Distributor & ‘Name That Tune’ Producer Was 97 View All November 4, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nick Hall Trevor Paul/Vice EXCLUSIVE : Nick Hall , who has exec produces series including The White Lotus and worked at companies including HBO, Amazon and A24, is getting into business with Vice Studios . Hall has struck a non-exclusive producing partnership with the company to develop and produce scripted projects through his Hallogram banner. It comes just over twelve months after the youth-skewing hipster media company hired former Paramount and Amazon exec Amy Powell as President of Vice Studios and landed a $75M credit facility to fill out its programming slate. Related Stories Executives Nick Hall Joins A24 To Oversee Creative For TV News Amazon MGM Studios Readies Guy Ritchie & Rob Williams London Crime Drama ‘Capital’ With Vice Studios & Jack Tar Pictures Attached As part of the deal, Hall will exec produce two projects currently in the works at Vice. Watch on Deadline He will exec produce the TV adaptation of Anika Jade Levy’s debut novel Flat Earth , which Levy is written with Pen15 co-creator Sam Zvibleman, and workplace comedy Work Husbands, which is loosely based on the real-life relationship of Gen Z marketers Nate Jones and Ziad Ahmed. In addition to exec producing season one of The White Lotus , which landed him an Emmy win in 2022, Hall has produced series including Luca Guadagnino’s We Are Who We Are for HBO and Sky Atlantic and FX’s The Shards as well as French-language series Icon of French Cinema , which was co-produced with A24 and Arte. After starting his career as an assistant at UTA and in comedy at Warner Bros., Hall spent seven years at HBO before moving to Amazon, where he oversaw comedy, drama and YA series. After a producing pact with HBO, he spent a year working as a TV executive at A24 . The move marks the latest programming move for the Gangs of London producer since Fortress Investment Group, Soros Fund Management and Monroe Capital acquired it out of bankruptcy for $225M in 2023. Projects include Capital , a crime drama series from Guy Ritchie in development at Amazon MGM Studios UK, scripted drama series in development with Pablo Torre about sports ownership, extreme wealth and corruption, and an adaptation of the video game franchise Payday with Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson. “Nick has a rare combination of great taste, strong instincts and the conviction to take creative risks,” said Amy Powell, President of Vice Studios. “He has an incredible ability to recognize and champion original voices and material that others might overlook. I’ve known Nick for many years, and I’ve always admired his commitment to filmmakers and stories that challenge expectations. His sensibility is a natural fit for Vice, and I’m excited to see what we create together.” Nick Hall added, “I feel incredibly fortunate to have worked with some of the most trailblazing leaders and culture-defining companies in television. I’m grateful for the opportunity to continue that tradition with Amy and Vice.” Hall is represented by attorney Jared Bloch. Bass & Raman In Dead Heat For L.A. Filmed over a sold-out run at Chicago’s Thalia Hall, the special navigates Soresi’s aspirations and anxieties around marriage and fatherhood, his skepticism about society’s substitutes for religion, and the double-edged sword of taking mental health seriously. This follows Soresi’s self-released 2025 hour Thief of Joy , which was widely praised as one of the year’s best. title: Voltage Pictures Gets ‘Nervous’ Around The World – AFM
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘La Bola Negra’ Caliente At Box Office With $43M Worldwide, Becomes Spain’s Top-Grossing Local Pic Of 2026 Blumhouse & Atomic Monster Unveil New Name For Combined Studio Lionsgate Teaming With Sony To Make Destin Daniel Cretton’s ‘Naruto’ View All November 4, 2026 8:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Nervous' Voltage EXCLUSIVE: Voltage Pictures has taken global rights (sans Korea) to the Sarah Bolger -starring psychological horror thriller Nervous , written and directed by Abner Pastoll ( A Good Woman Is Hard to Find , Road Games ). Sales are beginning on the title at the American Film Market. The pic also stars Ko Asung ( Snowpiercer , The Host ) and Sungsoo Yune ( Smugglers , Live Stream ). Voltage The plot: Desperate to save their crumbling marriage, Sarah and her husband relocate to the Korean countryside, where they discover a mysterious vinyl record that plays only silence. After listening, she loses the ability to hear men’s voices, plunging her into paranoia and hallucinations. Increasingly isolated and drawn to an enigmatic female neighbor, Sarah struggles to distinguish reality from nightmare. Is she losing her mind, or is something far more sinister at work? Related Stories News Trudie Styler Talks Journey To Directing 'Up Against It' & 'The Reception' Back-To-Back: "I'm In A Happy Place" News WTFilms Boards Italian Alps-Set Comedy-Thriller 'The Dregs' With Maddie Phillips & Stephen Lang - AFM The movie was shot in and around Seoul, with the project a South Korea-UK co-production from Story Robot and February Films, in association with Superbe Films and MAP, and in association with Solaire Partners and Central Investment Partners. Watch on Deadline The film is produced by Junyoung Jang and Pastoll, who also directs from a screenplay co-written with Richard Hobley. EPs are Guillaume Benski, Youngmin Kim and Sangjin Lee. The original score is composed by Matthew Pusti. “ Nervous represents the kind of bold, elevated horror that continues to resonate with global audiences,” said Alexandra Cocean, President International Sales and Distribution at Voltage Pictures. “Abner has crafted a provocative and deeply unsettling film that combines sophisticated psychological storytelling with striking visuals and an inventive use of sound. We are excited to screen the film to our buyers at AFM .” “ Nervous began with a simple but very unsettling idea: what happens when you can no longer hear the person closest to you?” said Junyoung Jang. “We wanted to explore that through sound and silence, creating something intimate, disorientating and cinematic. We’re thrilled to be partnering with Voltage to bring the film to audiences around the world and, for a film about silence, we’re excited to make some noise!” Nervous reps a reunion between Pastoll and Bolger following their collaboration on A Good Woman Is Hard to Find , which earned Bolger the Best Actress award at Screamfest. Nervous made its world premiere FrightFest 2026 as the opening-night film. It recently earned two honors at the 2026 Screamfest Horror Film Festival in Los Angeles, including Best Musical Score for Pusti and the inaugural ScareScore Biometric Best Picture Award. The movie is set to play MOTELX – Lisbon International Horror Film Festival, Fantasy Filmfest in Germany, Screamfest in Los Angeles, and the Festival International du Film de La Roche-sur-Yon in France, where it was selected for the Prix Variété competition. Additional selections include Belgium’s Razor Reel Flanders Film Festival, Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival in Estonia, and Japan’s YAMI Tokyo Horror Film Festival. title: Music Industry Moves: Jackson Wang Inks With WME; Position Music Signs Arkai to JV With Lindsey Stirling’s Label
full_text: × Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Nov 4, 2026 8:23am PT Music Industry Moves: Jackson Wang Inks With WME; Position Music Signs Arkai to JV With Lindsey Stirling’s Label By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Music Industry Moves: Jackson Wang Inks With WME; Position Music Signs Arkai to JV With Lindsey Stirling’s Label 31 minutes ago Justin Timberlake to Release Four-Part ‘Tell-All’ Docuseries, Featuring Janet Jackson, on Apple (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago Olivia Rodrigo, Katseye and Sienna Spiro to Be Honored at Variety’s 10th Annual Hitmakers Event 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Singer-songwriter Jackson Wang , currently starring in an Apple campaign tied to his new single and music video, “Thank You,” has signed with WME for representation. Wang’s 2019 debut album, “Mirrors,” became the first album by a solo Chinese artist to hit the Billboard Top 200 and over the years he has collaborated with Ciara, Swae Lee, Major Lazer, Gucci Mane, and others, and has headlined Los Angeles’s Kia Forum and Brooklyn’s Barclays Center; in 2022 he was the first Chinese solo artist to perform on the main stage at Coachella. In addition to WME, he continues to be represented by Team Wang Records and Roc Nation. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' + Position Music has signed Grammy-winning group Arkai to a JV label deal with Lindsey Stirling’s label LindseyStomp , through Position Music A&R, Jake Versluis. Described as “Hans Zimmer meets 2Cellos,” the Juilliard graduates have worked extensively in film and television, including the Emmy Awards, the Grammy Museum, the NBA Finals and others. Stirling says, “Arkai represents everything I hoped this label imprint could stand for: bold artistry, fearless creativity, and a willingness to push beyond the boundaries of genre. Jonathan and Philip are extraordinary musicians, but what excites me most is the heart and imagination they bring to everything they create. I couldn’t imagine better partners than Position Music to help us build a home where visionary artists can take big creative swings and bring their music to the world.” + Empire has announced two senior appointments in its New York office: Leesa Brunson-Boland as Senior Vice President, A&R Operations, and Bina Fronda as Senior Vice President, Marketing. Brunson previously served as Head of A&R Operations at 300 Entertainment following nearly two decades at Def Jam Recordings, where she worked with Rihanna, Jay-Z, Justin Bieber and Teyana Taylor. Fronda joins from Ultra Records where she was VP of Marketing, working closely with their artists such as Steve Aoki, Sofi Tukker and Benny Benassi. + British singer-songwriter Danny Griffiths has signed with Glassnote Records and released of his debut single, “Lightweight Champion,” which has been widely shared in demo form on social media. He is represented by Prolifica Management and Solo Agency Limited. Glassnote founder Daniel Glass says, “When we first heard Danny’s songs and then witnessed the passionate response from the audience each night he performs, we knew he belonged with us. It is always a dream to have so many respected industry people requesting a song that has not been released yet. Such is the case with ;Lightweight Champion,’ which, until now, only belonged to Danny Griffiths’ fans.” + Create Music Group has named Hayley Silvertown Chief Legal and Business Affairs Officer at the company. Based in the company’s Hollywood headquarters, Silvertown will oversee Create’s legal and business affairs functions and partner with the executive team on strategic transactions, investments and partnerships. She comes to Create from Paul Hastings where she was Of Counsel. She previously held roles at such firms as Willkie Farr & Gallagher and Shepard Mullin Richter and Hampton. She also worked in the business affairs departments of ICM and Warner Chappell music publishing. + Nebula17, the Los Angeles-based music and creative company founded by former Avex USA CEO Naoki Osada, has announced a major expansion of its executive team, publishing roster, label operations, and international initiatives. Daniel Hong joins Nebula17 as Chief Operating Officer, working alongside founder and CEO Naoki Osada on company strategy, operations, and growth while leading the company’s international division. He previously served as CEO of YG USA and COO of JYP USA, where he worked closely with globally successful acts including Blackpink, Stray Kids, and Girlset. Martha Blair Reynolds joins as Senior Director of Marketing, following her work at Ricky Reed’s Nice Life Recording Company. René Mark joins as Director of Digital with experience managing campaigns for BTS, Le Sserafim, and Tinashe at Interscope Geffen A&M and Nice Life Recording Company. Natalie Walsh joins as Director of A&R after working with Sabrina Claudio, Nasri, and Adam Messinger. Harukaze Wakabayashi joins as Senior Manager, International, from Warner Music Japan. Zac Cruz joins as A&R / Marketing Manager following roles at Avex and Revels Group, while Oscar Cornejo joins as Head Engineer, with credits including Grammy-winning work with Tyla and projects with Kanye West and Willow Smith. Nebula17 has also added three creators to its U.S. publishing roster: producer, musician, and sound designer Oh Gosh Leotus; Florida-born artist, songwriter, and producer Hydra; and producer Xansei. On the label side, Nebula17 has signed New York-based artist, producer, and musician Hojean. The company has also entered into a global distribution partnership with the Orchard. + Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (HBSE) has announced announced the hiring of Joe Giordano Jr. as Senior Vice President of Entertainment Booking. In this role, Joe will oversee entertainment booking for HBSE’s premier properties, including Prudential Center in Newark and Loew’s Jersey Theatre in Jersey City, and assist with the programming of other HBSE venues. “Joe’s deep experience in the entertainment industry and proven track record of building strong relationships while attracting major touring acts will be a tremendous asset to our team,” said Sean Saadeh, Chief Programming Officer and Head of Entertainment, Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment. “Joe has a rare ability to pair creative vision with instinctive talentspotting, consistently identifying and elevating entertainment experiences that resonate deeply with audiences.” Prior to becoming Oak View Group’s Vice President of Stadium, Arena and Theater Alliances, Giordano spent nearly a decade working for ASM Global (Legends), where he held national responsibilities in booking, and went on to serve as the Assistant General Manager at BOK Center in Tulsa, OK. + Oak View Group has announced a new agreement with Independent Artist Group (IAG) , to work with the agency’s music and comedy touring artists. title: NBCUniversal Invests in India Microdrama Producer in $80 Million Fundraising Round
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All November 4, 2026 8:21am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EloElo Group operates microdramas app Story TV. EloElo Group NBCUniversal and Hornbill Capital have led an $80 million Series C fundraising round for Indian microdrama producer EloElo Group, founded by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey. The new capital will allow the Story TV platform operator to produce new vertical dramas for export internationally, including to the U.S. market. The Series C investment, usually done to allow startups to scale operations, follows NBCUniversal’s Peacock streaming platform launching the unscripted vertical series, Campus Confidential: Miami , as part of a wider push into mobile content to reach new audiences. “At NBCUniversal, we see significant opportunity in mobile-first storytelling and emerging formats like micro dramas to engage audiences and meet evolving viewing habits. Under Saurabh’s leadership, EloElo has developed a differentiated, mobile-first approach with a clear focus on content and storytelling, positioning the company for long-term success. We’re excited to bring NBCUniversal’s global capabilities to the partnership as EloElo expands beyond India, including into the U.S. market,” Deepak Arya, executive vp of corporate strategy & development at NBCUniversal, said in a statement. EloElo Group, which launched in Bengaluru, India in 2020, points to an expanding slate of over 5000 micro dramas in six languages, while a Dolphin AI agentic production engine. Across its apps, EloElo Group added it has over 40 million monthly active users. “This Series C deepens our content across languages, with a sharper focus on premium originals, doubles down on Dolphin AI, and takes what we have built to more audiences and more markets,” Pandey, founder and CEO of EloElo Group, said in his own statement. Microdramas, which are typically produced in 60-90 second episodes and strategically written with a hook, a spike and a cliff hanger to get viewers onto the next episode, have caught on in North America and elsewhere internationally after coming out of China during the pandemic era. title: Toni Collette to Lead Apple TV Dramedy ‘Lenni’
full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 8:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Toni Collette Christian Hogstedt Logo text Apple TV ‘s latest series is going to opposite ends of the Earth for its inspiration and physical location. The streamer has picked up a dramedy called Lenni , with Toni Collette playing the title character. The series is based on a critically acclaimed Norwegian show, Pernille , and has started production in Australia, almost literally the other side of the world. In Lenni , Emmy winner Collette ( United States of Tara, Wayward ) will play a child welfare worker and divorced mother of two kids who “spends her days fighting for other people’s families while her own is in a constant state of hilarious chaos,” the logline reads. “The season follows Lenni through a new case, where the stakes couldn’t be higher as her work and personal life collides.” Related Stories TV 'Monarch: Legacy of Monsters' Eyes Season 3 Shakeup -- If It's Renewed Movies Ted McGinley Tapped to Narrate Volleyball Documentary 'Kings of the Beach' The cast also includes Ciarán Hinds, Dan Wyllie, Josh McKenzie, Celeste Barber, Genevieve Hegney, Arka Das and Wayne Blair. Made Up Stories and Keshet International are producing Lenni . Sarah Scheller ( Strife, The Letdown ) is adapting the Norwegian series, and Dearbhla Walsh ( Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Bad Sisters ) is directing. They executive produce with Bruna Papandrea, Steve Hutensky and Katie Amos of Made Up Stories, Avi Nir and Keren Shahar of Keshet International, and Collette. Also exec producing are Pernille creator Henriette Steenstrup, Bård Fjulsrud and Tanya Badendyck. Collette starred in Mae Martin’s Wayward on Netflix last year. Her other recent series credits include The Power at Prime Video, The Staircase at HBO Max and Pieces of Her at Netflix. title: Holocaust Drama ‘The Night Of Broken Glass’, With Clive Owen, Mélanie Laurent & Alexander Pettyfer, Gets North American Deal
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Holocaust Drama ‘The Night Of Broken Glass’, With Clive Owen, Mélanie Laurent & Alexander Pettyfer, Gets North American Deal Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger & Nico Greetham Join Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell In ‘Survive: The Game’ Indie Film Fund Archetype Media Finance Launches With Nicolas Cage & Lucy Hale Films Among First Projects View All November 4, 2026 8:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clive Owen in 'The Night Of Broken Glass' first look International Film Trust EXCLUSIVE : Quiver Distribution has acquired the North American rights to The Night of Broken Glass , the historical drama based on true events, directed by Oscar-winning filmmaker Stefan Ruzowitzky ( The Counterfeiters ). As we’ve previously reported, the film from Dor Film, Benaroya Pictures and The Launch Company stars BAFTA and Golden Globe winner Clive Owen ( Children of Men ), Mélanie Laurent ( Inglourious Basterds ) and Alexander Pettyfer ( The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare ). Related Stories News Jean-Claude Van Damme Returning To Martial Arts Roots In Yakuza Action Pic ‘Katana’ For Jeremy Zag & The Veterans — AFM Casting Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger & Nico Greetham Join Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell In ‘Survive: The Game’ Written by Jonathan Frank, Scott Mann, Uli Edel and Julius Grützke, Quiver will release the film theatrically in North America on January 29. Historical thriller The Night of Broken Glass , based on the events of Kristallnacht, is “set in Berlin, in November 1938. Following the assassination of a German diplomat in Paris, Nazi propaganda exploits the incident to unleash a wave of violence against the Jewish population. As mobs storm Jewish neighborhoods and places of worship, Police Lieutenant Wilhelm Krützfeld (Owen) and his partner, Kai Lehmann (Pettyfer), investigate the murder of a Jewish doctor amid the escalating chaos. With orders to stand down as the city descends into violence, Krützfeld finds himself increasingly torn between his duty to the regime and his own sense of right and wrong. Over the course of one harrowing night, he must confront his conscience, find the courage to act on his convictions and decide whether he is willing to risk everything to do what is right.” Watch on Deadline “ The Night of Broken Glass is a powerful and gripping film about a defining moment in history, and the courage it takes to stand against injustice. With antisemitism once again on the rise around the world, this story feels particularly urgent and relevant. Stefan Ruzowitzky has crafted a compelling thriller that reminds us how quickly hatred can take hold, and how the choices of individuals can make a difference. As we mark International Holocaust Remembrance Day, we are proud to bring this timely and important film to theaters across North America,” said Quiver Co-Presidents Jeff Sackman and Berry Meyerowitz. “Making The Night of Broken Glass was an opportunity to revisit a defining moment in history and examine the human choices made in its midst. I wanted to approach the story with respect for the historical realities while exploring the characters and the decisions they face. I hope the film encourages audiences to reflect on how prejudice and hatred take hold, and on the importance of standing against injustice,” added director Stefan Ruzowitzky. title: What Abdul El-Sayed’s Wild, Historic Ride to the Senate Means to One Michigander
full_text: × Skip to main content By Mikey O'Connell Plus Icon Mikey O'Connell Senior Entertainment Editor View All November 4, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dr. Abdul El-Sayed Salwan Georges/Getty Images I’m just a Great Lakes boy, standing in front of his home state, asking for some clarity. And, perhaps, I’m a little closer to getting some. Dr. Abdul El-Sayed , the Michigan native fond of exercising the right to bare (his impressive) arms , has just won my home state’s messy Senate race by six points. This is a boon to Democrats’ legislative goals — and to my own mental health. Because, in an admittedly myopic move, I decided early on that he would be the one candidate to whom I’d pin all of my 2026 hopes. Not just because he’s a litmus test for non-coastal Americans’ appetite for progressive politics. Because I deeply needed to know if my complicated home state was capable of electing a loud, liberal, practicing Muslim to such a high office. Related Stories News Trump Crashes Out After Democrats Flip House and Senate, Slams Fox News and Texas' Greg Abbott News Elon Musk Responds After His Record $474 Million Bet on Republicans Ends in Blowout My doubts were not without merit. I spent my adolescence in deep red Livingston County, in a smallish town with exceptional public schools and a storybook Main Street that now has shops that sport trans pride flags in their widows and hosts an annual and very well-attended Gilmore Girls festival. Last December, mid-Hanukkah, that same Main Street was bombarded with white supremacists carrying signs that read “Happy Holidays, Heil Hitler” while reportedly spicing up their antisemitic campaign by calling passing holiday shoppers the n-word and the f-slur. Mike Rogers, El-Sayed’s MAGA-endorsed opponent, grew up in Livingston County as well. And he represented our town during his years in the Michigan State Senate before going on to represent those same constituents in the House of Representatives. My dad couldn’t stand him. Still can’t. And I vividly recall rolling my eyes under the brim of my marching band hat (it’s called a Shako!), whenever I had to watch Rogers gladhand the town’s Republican majority at football games as he made his leap to national politics. What I wouldn’t learn for another 25 years is that El-Sayed’s grandparents were helping to raise Abdul just a few miles away. Because Livingston County is also home to Jan and Judy Johnson, the newly famous TV stars whose series of campaign spots for their grandson epitomize the kind of Michiganders who I know and come from. OK, that was arguably too much color about one random cluster of towns an hour’s drive west of Detroit. But if this much paradox can exist within this 15-mile radius, how can anything but an election like the one we’ve just had tell me where the majority of people’s heads and hearts are at? Because I didn’t grow up in the only culturally bipolar part of Michigan or any other state. This country is a real trip, and most of us realized that before 2016. I’m back in Michigan a lot, just last week in fact, but I haven’t voted there for almost 20 years. Another thing I have in common with Mike Rogers is that I spend most of my time in another place. California, for me. And watching so much of this race from afar has been a tough hang. El-Sayed regularly had to endure a gun-toting pardoned Jan. 6 insurrectionist crashing his rallies. He had to navigate his proximity to the national sideshow that is Hasan Piker. His campaign was wildly outspent by the Rogers one, which blanketed the airwaves with some exceptionally racist content. And, on the eve of the election, El-Sayed’s primary opponent, Haley Stevens, distracted from the conversation with her left-field endorsement of Rogers that may have ejected her from the Democratic party and possibly a political career. If it isn’t clear by this point, I am aligned with El-Sayed on many issues. I made a few modest donations to his campaign. I’ve been wearing a baseball cap with his name on it most weekends since before the primary. I sent his spoof of the So You Think You Can Leave sketch to everyone I’ve ever met. But, for me, I didn’t really need to know if Michigan was ready to go full liberal. I just wanted some assurance, in this grotesque circus of a race, that the majority of those in the complex and diverse place that I still consider home could recognize what I believe to be a good man in some slightly different packaging. Everybody likes to invoke the whole “As [insert state here] goes, so goes the nation” thing. Wow, humble much? If that was ever even true on an electoral level, I don’t believe it is any longer. But it can be on a personal one. Because as Michigan goes, so goes my optimism for America’s future. And today, I feel a little bit better on that front. This is part of The Hollywood Reporter’s ongoing midterm coverage. You can check out all of our pieces here . THR

title: Big Daddy: How Jordan Firstman Turned ‘Club Kid’ Into a Glorious, Gay, Oscar-Worthy Crowdpleaser
full_text: Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Max Montgomery for Variety It’s 3 p.m. at the Sunset Tower Hotel, the purgatory hour between lunch and dinner at one of Hollywood’s favorite places to hammer out deals and gaze at stars. Jordan Firstman decides it’s late enough in the day for his first Aperol spritz, which leads to some reminiscing. It was a decade ago that über-producer Greg Berlanti invited the then-25-year-old Firstman to the Tower Bar to discuss the trajectory of his career. Berlanti, who became the showrunner of “Dawson’s Creek” at age 27, has served as a coach for more than one young queer creator, and Firstman had just sold a series to the cable channel Sundance TV, based on his romantic intergenerational short film “Call Your Father.” He was getting pushback from the network about casting a 50-year-old out gay actor in the lead. Max Montgomery for Variety “He wasn’t an unknown; he was a great working actor,” Firstman recalls, declining to give his name. “The studio was like, ‘We would love to cast a gay actor, but there’s just no one that even touches the level of fame we need to justify you doing the show at this budget.’” Firstman stabs Aperol-soaked ice with his straw, tensing at the memory. “I got to a place where I told them, ‘I’m not doing this if the actor isn’t gay.’ I was a little bit threatening, like, ‘You guys don’t want to look homophobic.’” Sundance TV ended up passing on the show, prompting Berlanti to attempt to rescue it for the nascent HBO Max. It would languish there for years, and then disappear altogether in that company’s revolving door of mergers and executive changes. My, how times have changed. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' Firstman, 35, does not resemble the typical filmmaker whose career launched into the stratosphere out of the Cannes Film Festival. His baggy jeans, chest-hugging polo and Oakley raver sunglasses lend themselves better to the hipster neighborhood of Silver Lake. (Not coincidentally, that’s the setting of Rachel Sennott’s HBO comedy “I Love L.A.,” on which he co-stars as a stylist and BFF to Sennott’s aspiring talent manager, Maia.) Impishness is Firstman’s trademark — he’s all easy crooked smiles and bouncing brown curls. That quality is what’s made his “Internet Gay” persona travel so readily — as evidenced by his more than 1 million followers on Instagram and TikTok. Yet in May, Firstman took the French Riviera by storm with “ Club Kid ” — his feature debut as a writer-director and first turn as a leading man on the big screen — where the project inspired a heated bidding war. Indie giant A24 beat out Focus Features, Searchlight, Netflix and Mubi for a global rights deal worth $17 million, instantly solidifying Firstman as a force to be reckoned with. “Club Kid” tells the story of nightlife promoter Peter (Firstman), who has blinked and lost 10 years of his life to hard partying (ketamine, cocaine and GHB are supporting characters in the film), a circuit of on-demand lovers and a deep indulgence in modern queer life in New York City. Depression and low self-esteem hover over Peter like buzzing drones, swatted away by late nights and early mornings and Uber Eats and laptop porn. That cycle is disrupted when 10-year-old Arlo (newcomer Reggie Absolom) shows up at the door of Peter’s SoHo apartment announcing he is his son. Both father and child are saved and tested in equal parts, as we learn that truly happy endings never come home with us from the club. The magic trick of “Club Kid” is Firstman’s ability to sell a broad, humorous story about the kind of love that fundamentally changes us — all while being firmly rooted in the digital, unapologetically gay culture that formed his artistic sensibilities. Firstman is the creative love child of Judd Apatow and Nicole Holofcener, delivered unto a Gen Z cohort who’ve become obsessed with watching movies in theaters. “It’s been amazing to see the kinds of people that relate to this film, but it really is a movie about growth,” says Firstman. “In Telluride, I watched a 75-year-old conservative man leave the theater in tears. Then we took it to the New York Film Festival, which I was very nervous to do, and showed it to the 35-year-olds who do drugs. I built the story to work on levels, with the top being a layer of warmth that feels like a hug. I explore some of my more transgressive ideas beneath the surface. If you don’t get it, there’s still a story that will make you laugh and feel something.” For those not familiar with Firstman, he’ll seem like an overnight sensation. To others, he’s a veteran comedic force for the chronically online. From the tiny town of Northport on the North Shore of Long Island, Firstman made the pilgrimage to Manhattan that countless hopeful queer people had before him. While building his social following with razor-sharp snark, Firstman worked in writers’ rooms for cult comedy series such as “The Other Two,” “Search Party” and “Big Mouth.” He also wrote a now-legendary sketch for Aubrey Plaza when she hosted the 2020 Independent Spirit Awards, highlighting gay representation among that year’s nominees that might not be obvious to the straight eye; it ended up becoming a tribute to an astonished Laura Dern, who tearfully stood up and cheered. Max Montgomery for Variety Starting out, Firstman didn’t dare dream of ascending the stairs to the Grand Palais or carving a path to the Oscars stage. “It was the era of the TV auteurs,” he says of his early idols. “Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Donald Glover, Lena Dunham: I had a voice and felt confident I could do that. They are storytellers. The directing part has always been scary to me, because I’m not as versed in images. I’m the person at the museum who has to ask why the painting is good. Words are the way I get my point across.” Firstman overcame that fear to shoot “Club Kid” in just 26 days last year. With a production budget just shy of $5 million, Firstman sacrificed his own fees as writer, director and star in exchange for two nonnegotiables: There had to be a pivotal location shoot in London, and the movie had to be shot on pricey film stock — a decision he defends with the weariness of a seasoned auteur. “That was vital; we shot on 35mm. We want prints of this movie made,” he says with a kind of reverence. Not for his own ego, but for his vision of how “Club Kid” needs to exist in the world of cinema. Two-time Oscar nominee and longtime Firstman mentor Richard LaGravenese (“The Fisher King,” “Behind the Candelabra”) isn’t surprised the debut director is calling his own shots. “What makes Jordan special is that, like any good artist, you don’t wait for an invitation,” LaGravenese says. “You create the space for yourself in the culture. He’s done it by sticking to who he is.” When I spoke with Firstman at Cannes after “Club Kid” exploded, he told me that the script began as a frothy experiment meant to evoke the dreamy wish-fulfillment films of the early aughts like “Uptown Girls,” starring Brittany Murphy, and “Big Daddy” from Adam Sandler. “That’s how I was pitching it, and once I started writing, it got a little ‘Kramer vs. Kramer,’” he said. The movie also had to be decidedly, gloriously gay. It’s not lost on Firstman that “Club Kid” sits alongside other 2026 releases that represent some of the most elevated queer stories that mainstream Hollywood has produced in years, with several of them sitting in the awards conversation with Firstman’s film: Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s “La Bola Negra,” Andrew Scott’s tearjerker “Elsinore,” Jane Schoenbrun’s “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” and Lukas Dhont’s fellow Cannes player “Coward.” Queerness is integral to these movies, but not exclusively the point — they are portraits of soldiers propping up unjust wars, artists defying heteronormative conventions to find themselves and, in Firstman’s case, a fading party boy belatedly becoming an adult. Max Montgomery for Variety “I feel like there hasn’t been a defined generation of new filmmakers since the Safdie brothers era began,” Firstman says. “Los Javis and Jane and Lukas and I are all around the same age. Our collective is so queer, and people are responding, and the movies are doing well.” At the Tower Bar, we cave and order french fries to soak up the spritzes. Firstman is recognized by a musclebound music producer dining nearby with a woman of equitable attractiveness. “He’s hot,” Firstman says, “but he’s a really nice guy. And he has a great kid!” If Firstman is indeed part of a new wave of queer storytellers, some might say it took a minute for him to ingratiate himself to that community. Prior to his Cannes breakthrough, his brand was, well, messy. Firstman excels at highlighting the absurdity of celebrity and the pretension of coastal media types. Last year, he criticized the crossover sensation “Heated Rivalry” for what he called a narrow depiction of gay sex (he said that’s “not how gay people fuck,” and that the show eroticized two closeted athletes falling in love under deep cover). The show’s rabid fans descended, and Firstman made it right by deploying his online instincts and recruiting “Heated Rivalry” star Hudson Williams for a TikTok post satirizing the whole blowup. In the clip, Williams lip-synched Nicki Minaj’s 2015 MTV VMAs acceptance speech, in which she aggressively called out host Miley Cyrus for remarks she’d made about the rapper in an interview (“Miley, what’s good?”). Firstman played Cyrus, claiming she’d been taken out of context. This Minaj-Cyrus exchange also appears in “Club Kid,” as Firstman’s character sells drugs to a group of shrill gay guys locked in a bathroom stall. Much of the press tour for “Club Kid” has been a reframing of Firstman’s intentions, especially as it relates to his fellow queer people. “You really can’t try to steer the narrative within the gay community. But I’m speaking to them from my heart, and I feel confident in what I’m showing them. I’m also doing my best to be a good friend, and to protect my cast,” he says. “It’s been amazing seeing messages from people who say they feel seen by the movie — even the judgy-ass bitches in the nightlife community. They were like, ‘ You did that .’” Josh Hutcherson, Firstman’s co-star on “I Love L.A.,” who describes him as his brother, says the filmmaker is “one of the most sensitive people I know. He has an abrasive and controversial mask he wears, and it’s very funny. His humor shakes up the right people. But he’s also got an amazing sensor for humanity.” That “Club Kid” leads with its heart might confound Firstman observers, but the movie’s sentimental value is why A24 made its big bet. Because on the other side of that LBTGQIA+ embrace is the rest of the moviegoing market, and the eight-figure check cut by the boutique studio means “Club Kid” must leg out at the box office through the holiday season and beyond to reach profitability, after opening in limited release this weekend. Firstman is personally involved in the marketing, recruiting famous DJs to spin at premiere parties in Paris, Rome, London and New York, while rolling out merchandise like “Club Kid” cropped T-shirts that resemble one his character wears in the film (“I Love Björk and Bareback,” it reads). Some of his peers have suffered the slings and arrows of failed crossovers. In 2022, Universal Pictures backed comedian Billy Eichner’s noble attempt to program a gay romantic comedy for wide audiences in the Apatow-produced “Bros.” That film grossed only $14 million worldwide on a $22 million budget, not accounting for the significant marketing cash the studio spent. While Firstman’s film is quite different, the projects may invite an inevitable comparison. Max Montgomery for Variety A24 and Firstman are betting on word-of-mouth, which also has its consequences. Conservative rage-baiters could latch on to “Club Kid” for its depiction of a child spun into the chaos of a druggy NYC underbelly. The film’s 100% Fresh Rotten Tomatoes score (based on 65 reviews), however, is a good indicator that audiences are receiving Firstman’s intended message. After all, the kid in “Club Kid” is often the one doing the child-rearing. “The world of this movie isn’t sensationalized: I don’t put a positive or negative lens on the party scene. I just try to show these people for their beauty and their flaws and their creativity,” says Firstman. “I wanted to explore what felt universal. A general millennial malaise, like, what are we doing? The pandemic was six years ago, and we still feel like we’re in our 20s — but we’re not. This has permeated our culture. So many friends of mine wanted to stop partying and didn’t know how.” But for a movie about generational sadness, “Club Kid” is riotously funny, filled with Easter eggs for meme lovers and culture queens. During a dance sequence, Firstman and a friend do choreography to the chant “No arms! No legs! No eyes!,” a reference to a 1998 micro-scandal caused by Claire Danes, who used those words to describe the people she saw in the Philippines while filming the prison drama “Brokedown Palace.” (When a character expresses confusion about the dance, Peter screams, “Google ‘Claire Danes Philippines!’”) One of the film’s best jokes was sacrificed for a leaner run time, Firstman laments. On his second day of daddy duty, Peter takes little Arlo to brunch at the glitterati staple Balthazar. He asks if his son, born and raised in the U.K., likes the spot because it was founded by another Brit (celebrity chef Keith McNally). Peter jokes that “James Corden isn’t even allowed in here anymore,” referencing a nasty 2022 beef between McNally and the late-night host over the latter’s alleged rudeness to the staff. “Who is James Corden?” the boy asks. Peter sighs with jealousy and tells the kid he’s so lucky not to know. Max Montgomery for Variety “If I want a bunch of gays to be screaming the Nicki Minaj speech, the gays will like that. But a straight guy will still get the message — you’re trapped in the bathroom with annoying gays,” Firstman says with a laugh. There’s also the script’s parade of memorable nicknames for drug use, with “Sniffany Haddish” as the moniker for cocaine. Want to mix that with ketamine? Then you’re having “a little Charlie, a little Kirk.” Administering your drugs in the rectum for faster results? That’s a “Benson Boof.” A millennial born on the tail end of his generation, Firstman grew up with the competitive noise of friends posting their best, most successful lives minute by minute on social media. As the sweet orange liquid in our glasses turns to slush, he says he’s grateful that fame and artistic praise didn’t come so fast or easy. Whatever fate the box office and the Oscars hold for “Club Kid” and Firstman, he’s leveled up as both an artist and a man. “Life gives you what it gives you when it does,” he says, imagining a world where that Sundance TV show had actually been made. “I don’t know where I’d be now. My voice and vision are more fully formed because of my experience.” At the last second, I try to tempt Firstman with another round, but he declines. After all, he’s on his way to the first L.A. screening of his film, to be moderated by “Anora” Oscar winner Sean Baker. He bids me farewell when, half in his car, Firstman springs out and runs back to the valet stand. “This is for you,” he says, handing me a lighter emblazoned with the words “Club Kid.” Location: Roleplay Design showroom; Styling: Chloe and Chenelle/A Frame Agency; Grooming: Kristen Shaw/A Frame Agency/St. Meto; Look 1 (Black Suit): Full look: Gucci; Look 2 (Blue Shirt): Full look: Tom Ford; Watch: Tiffany; Look 3 (Black Jacket with White Shirt): Jacket, shirt and tie: Dolce & Gabbana; Look 4 (Black Sweater): Sweater: Prada; Jeans: All Saints Loading comments... full_text: × Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Nov 4, 2026 8:00am PT Former OnlyFans Star Camilla Araújo Sets ‘Plot Twist’ Podcast Launch in New Expansion Into Long-Form Entertainment By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Former OnlyFans Star Camilla Araújo Sets ‘Plot Twist’ Podcast Launch in New Expansion Into Long-Form Entertainment 33 minutes ago Stocks Rally Higher After Democrats Flip Congress 2 hours ago Democrats Win House and Senate in Sweeping Rout of GOP 12 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Camilla Araújo Camilla Araújo, a YouTuber, entrepreneur and former OnlyFans creator, is launching her next endeavor: “Plot Twist,” a new weekly interview podcast series featuring guests from pop culture and beyond. “Plot Twist” episodes will premiere on Araújo’s YouTube channel, which has more than 9.3 million subscribers, and will also be available across major podcast platforms. Short-form clips and highlights will be distributed across her social media channels, reaching her combined audience of more than 27 million followers. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' “I’ve spent the last few years building my career in front of millions of people, and along the way I’ve met so many other incredible creators who are doing the same,” Araújo said in a statement provided to Variety . “The one thing I’ve realized is that there is always so much more to who someone is than what you see online. That’s why I created ‘Plot Twist’: to get in there and have real conversations that go beyond the clickbait and the headlines.” According to Araújo, on her podcast, she will focus on talking about “all the reasons why getting out of the box is the actual key to creative and financial freedom.” “I want to talk about those unseen moments, those hidden fears, and those crazy decisions that led people to really become who they are now,” she said. “Everyone’s life is full of unexpected plot twists, and this is the place where we’re going to talk about them. Let’s fucking go!” Araújo was born in Raleigh, North Carolina, to Brazilian immigrant parents. The 24-year-old first rose to prominence following her appearance in MrBeast’s record-breaking “Squid Game” recreation in 2021. That same year, she joined OnlyFans and won a massive following — writing in a social media post that she earned more than $11.5 million from the site in 2025. In a January 2026 video, Araújo announced that she was leaving OnlyFans to start Becoming Her, a paid online social media mentorship course “exposing the viral content formula I used to make millions from my phone and how you can steal it.” According to Araújo’s reps, her “Plot Twist” podcast is centered on the idea that no one should be defined by a single label. Each episode will feature conversations with celebrities, entrepreneurs and cultural figures about the pivotal moments, unexpected challenges and personal decisions that shaped their careers. Recording for “Plot Twist” is scheduled to start before the end of 2026, with a premiere date TBD. The podcast will be produced by Elan Gale through his unscripted production company, TheYearOfElan, and shot in person at Main Character Studios in Miami. In addition to launching “Plot Twist,” Araújo has additional products and business ventures in development. She also has used her platform to support charitable causes and community-driven fundraising initiatives, including animal welfare efforts. ‘Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Trailer: The Wilderness Survivors Return Home Loading comments...

title: Bri Lee’s Novel ‘The Work’ Set For TV Adaptation At Dollhouse Pictures
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Kartik Aaryan To Star In ‘Ladaku’ With Kabir Khan Directing; Worldwide Release Date Set For 2027 ‘Colin From Accounts’ Maker Easy Tiger Adapting Dervla McTiernan Novel ‘Three Reasons For Revenge’ As TV Series ‘Black Snow’: Travis Fimmel Is Back On Cold Case Trail In Teaser For Season 3; Premiere Date Set In Australia View All November 4, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Work' is being developed for TV Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Bri Lee ‘s Australian bestseller The Work is getting a TV adaptation. Dollhouse Pictures – the Sydney-based production collective led by Rose Byrne, Krew Boylan, Shannon Murphy and Jessica Carrera – landed the screen option on the novel following a negotiation with rights holder UTA. Published by Allen & Unwin, The Work is set between New York, Brisbane and Sydney and follows Lally, an ambitious New York gallerist, and Patrick, a Sydney-based junior antiques appraiser, two young professionals, both desperately trying to establish themselves in the contemporary art world. Related Stories News Rose Byrne's Dollhouse Pictures Teams With Foundation Media Partners On Film Adaptation Of Anh Do's Novel 'Wolf Girl' Casting Rose Byrne's First Production From Her Dollhouse Pictures, 'Seriously Red', Underway; Will Star With Bobby Cannavale, Krew Boylan & More Per the synopsis, “When they meet, their chemistry is instant, beginning a turbulent long distant relationship. As their personal and professional lives become increasingly entangled, they begin to question if their love can survive distance, ambition and their cut-throat workplace.” Watch on Deadline Screenwriter Hannah Lehmann , who created and directed Snap original series Two Sides , is creating the TV series, with Lee and Carerra the executive producers. Screen Australia is supporting development. “I’ve always admired Bri Lee’s writing and her willingness to question power, privilege and the institutions that shape us,” said Carrera. “What excites me about The Work is its seductive world, where everything has a value and the rules are constantly shifting. At its heart is a complicated relationship that asks what if the person you desire most is also the person who costs you the most. Hannah Lehmann brings a sharp and assured voice to the adaptation.” Dollhouse’s productions include Dolly Parton biopic Seriously Red . Other titles on the slate include the first adaptation of Anh Do’s Wolf Girl , which we first reported on in October 2024. Lee said The Work had found “a production and writing team that are committed to making this show properly gutsy, hella sexy, and seriously funny.” She added the novel “was always so cinematic in my head, and Dollhouse Productions are going to take the words off the page and build a magnetic, can’t-look-away spectacle. Hannah is a genius who understands these characters’ deepest fears and desires.” Lee is represented by UTA and Grace Heifetz at a4 Literary. Her other books include non-fiction titles Eggshell Skull , Beauty and Who Gets to Be Smart , and literature publication News & Reviews . Her second novel, Seed , was published last year. title: Trump Crashes Out After Democrats Flip House and Senate, Slams Fox News and Texas’ Greg Abbott
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 7:33am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Donald Trump Alex Wong/Getty Images After Democrats flipped the U.S. House and Senate on Tuesday night, it’s safe to say President Donald Trump wasn’t too thrilled. Hours after the polls closed and it was revealed that Democrats won some surprising races in the 2026 midterms, including for the Texas, South Carolina and North Carolina Senate, Trump took to Truth Social hours after the polls closed with several posts, slamming Fox News and Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who lost re-election to Democrat Gina Hinojosa . “If Greg Abbott, the Governor of Texas, hadn’t become a RINO in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost,” he wrote in one post. “He went back to his original formula, and it wasn’t pretty!” Related Stories News Elon Musk Responds After His Record $474 Million Bet on Republicans Ends in Blowout Midterms 2026 Hollywood Sat Out the Billionaire-Tax Fight. Its Workers Could Pay the Price. Trump added in another, “Why does FoxNews have Bill de Blasio, the Worst Mayor in the History of New York City, on air, ranting and raving like a Lunatic? He left the City in disgrace, and the damage he caused was incalculable — It has never been the same, and now he’s telling us how to run America. FoxNews bears responsibility for these losses by constantly and consistently putting on the Dumocrat opposition, and worse. GOD BLESS AMERICA!” Along with posting a photo of his signature red caps, with the word “VETO” displayed on it, he also wrote , “I’m going to become a Political Pundit, both good and bad, on the reasons these Candidates won and lost!” Earlier in the evening, as it started to become clear that it was going to be a big night for Democrats, Trump initially claimed that he would have won in a landslide if his name was on the ballot. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” he wrote on Truth Social. However, Trump wasn’t eligible to be on the 2026 ballot as he’s currently the sitting president of the United States. He also can’t run again in 2028, as the 22nd Amendment of the U.S. Constitution limits any person to being elected to the presidency twice, and Trump was already elected in 2016 and 2024. While Trump appears furious at the midterm results, he also told The New York Times shortly before 10:30 p.m. on Tuesday that he’s “absolutely willing to accept” them. The president added to the Times , “We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out.” THR

title: Thomasin McKenzie, Finn Cole and Antony Starr to Lead ‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest,’ Logical and Protagonist Launching at AFM (EXCLUSIVE)

As per the synopsis: “But what begins as one desperate lie will inadvertently change the course of the legend forever.” “‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest’ is a radical new take of one of the world’s most enduring legends, reinvented as a bold, visceral and relentlessly propulsive film,” said Dave Bishop, CEO of Protagonist Pictures. “Patrick Vollrath will deliver an electrifying cinematic vision to a story that turns mythology on its head, combining gripping set pieces with genuine moral complexity.” Added Andrei Kamarowsky, head of international at Logical Pictures Group: “What immediately drew us to ‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest’ was the ingenuity and novelty of its premise: one young woman’s desperate deception sets Robin Hood and his outlaws on a dangerous journey that will ultimately reshape the myth.
